Historian {{ill|John Breen (scholar)|Q6223046|qid=Q6223046}} points out that the current deities enshrined at the Sanno Seven Shrines were devised by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shigekuni Kishita}}, and they first appeared in a document called ``Enshrined Deities and Kansho Nenki etc.'' submitted to Otsu Prefecture in early 1888.{{Sfn|Breen|2009|pp=159-160}}.Shigekuni Kishita says that the deity enshrined at Ninomiya is Oyamakui's Wakon, and the enshrined deity at Ushionomiya is Oyamakui's Aratama, and Yukimaru Shogenji's theory that ``Kohieizan Daimyojin'' was enshrined in the shadow of Mt. Hachioji even before Ōki no Kami was enshrined at Mt. Even before the deity of Mt. Miwa was enshrined, it was worshiped in the shadow of Mt. Hachioji, and this Kohiei Daimyojin is considered to be {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kunijotateson}}, the first deity after the creation of heaven and earth, and the name of Oyamakui is not seen {{Sfn|Breen|2009|pp=148-149}}. }} In addition, it is thought to be influenced by Norinaga Motoori's {{ill|Mitama|Q495568|qid=Q495568}} theory and the claim that Oyamakui and Tamayorihime are a married couple.{{Sfn|Breen|2009|pp=159-160}}. Norinaga Motoori does not mention the mutual relationship between the four shrines of Hachioji, Sannomiya, Ninomiya, and Juzenshi at all {{Sfn|Breen|2009|pp=159-160}}. Shigekuni Kishita also wrote ``{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}'' and {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ar|موتوري نوريناغا|bg|Мотоори Норинага|de|Motoori Norinaga|es|Motoori Norinaga|fa|موتوئوری نوریناگا|fi|Motoori Norinaga|fr|Motoori Norinaga|gl|Motoori Norinaga|hu|Motoori Norinaga|it|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長|ka|მოტოორი ნორინაგა|ko|모토오리 노리나가|lt|Norinaga Motoori|mt|Motoori Norinaga|pl|Norinaga Motoori|pt|Motoori Norinaga|ro|Motoori Norinaga|ru|Мотоори Норинага|simple|Motoori Norinaga|sl|Motoori Norinaga|th|โมโตริ โนรินางะ|uk|Мотоорі Норінаґа|zh|本居宣長|qid=Q384647}}'s ``{{ill|Kojiki|qid=Kojiki|lt=Kojiki}}''. Oyamakui was enshrined as the deity based on the ``Kiden|Q11410835}}'', but Tagoko Hime-jin, the deity enshrined at {{ill|Munakata Shrines|Q11451876|qid=Q11451876}}, {{j alink|Hakusan Hime Shrine|Q704702|Hakusan Hime Shrine}} is the enshrined deity, Hakusan Hime ({{ill|Kikurihime|Q11619891|qid=Q11619891|lt=Kikuri Himegami}}) Neither appear in "Kojiki" or "Kojikiden" {{Sfn|Breen|2009|p=160}}{{Sfn|Breen|2009|p=172}}. The shrines in the current Higashihongu shrine grounds are described as ``Oyamakui no Kami's gods that guide the family and life.'' John Breen sees the interrelationship of the four shrines of Hachioji, Sannomiya, Ninomiya, and Juzenji as a product of Shigekuni's imagination, saying, ``In any case, it is these gods (invented by Shigekuni) that are currently being worshiped at Hiyoshi Taisha Shrine. And it can be said with certainty that these gods were ``created'' with the Meiji Restoration.''{{Sfn|Breen|2009|pp=159-160}}Boleyn states that although ``Enshrined Deities and Kanjo Nenki'' appear to be fabrications by Shigekuni Kishita, they can also be understood as the result of his search for the true identity of Hiyoshi Shrine in order to return it to its original appearance and its original enshrined deities.{{Sfn|Breen|2009|pp=159-160}} Boleyn also speculates that Shigekuni Kishita may have thought that the shrine was a suitable shrine for Tamayorihime, who had picked up an arrow in the Kamogawa River, since there was a spiritual spring right below the shrine.{{Sfn|Breen|2009|pp=159-160}}. Boleyn considers that the basis for Shigekuni Kishita's claims other than Kui Oyama's appearance in Kojiki is weak or nonexistent {{Sfn|Breen|2009|p=161}}. It was believed that this was based on a historical document called ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hiyoshi Shane Iguchi Densho}}'' which was written in the 16th century by Yukimaru Ikube, who wrote about the history of the 11th century, but some people, such as {{ill|Kōjun Fukui|Q11591380|qid=Q11591380}}, said that it did not seem to be a historical document from that time. It is known that this is a fake book created by a person believed to be Shigekuni Kishita at the end of the Edo period and during the Meiji Restoration.{{Sfn|Breen|2009|p=161}}{{Sfn|Yoshida |2024|p=190}}{{Efn|The second part (of Masato Sato's ``Research on Hiyoshi Shrine and Sanno Shinto'') examines the establishment of the Sanno Shinto canon and its forgeries. The first chapter is a major accomplishment in questioning the ``Hiyoshisha Negiguchi Densho'', which is considered to be the oldest book on the theory of the Hiyoshi shrine enshrined deity, based on an examination of various books, and denying the authenticity of this book by providing evidence that it was written between the end of the early modern period and the beginning of the Meiji period. ” (Chief reviewer: Waseda University Faculty of Letters, Arts and Sciences, Professor {{ill|Ryōshun Ōkubo|Q11432057|qid=Q11432057}}, Reviewer: Waseda University Faculty of Letters, Arts and Sciences, Professor {{ill|Kenjirō Tsuchida|Q11423791|qid=Q11423791}}, Kokugakuin University Professor Emeritus/Visiting Professor {{ill|Okada Chuangji|Q20039179|qid=Q20039179}}）<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abstract of Doctoral (Literature) Dissertation Review Report “Research on Hiyoshi Shrine and Sanno Shinto”|author Masato Sato=|url=http://hdl.handle.net/2065/00074133|website=Waseda University Repository |publisher=Waseda University |date= |access-date=2025-05-17 }}</ref>}}. All descriptions of the gods that Shigekuni Shigekuni enshrined, including Oyamakui, are based on the ``Hiyoshisha Negiguchi Densho,'' and Boleyn commented, ``This forgery called the ``Hiyoshisha Negikuchi Densho'' must be seen as a great success.'' {{Sfn|Breen|2009|p=172}}, Prior to Masato Sato's research, ``Hiyoshisha Negiguchi Densho'' was generally believed to be from before the medieval period, and since the Meiji period, it has been used as the basis for claiming that the deity enshrined at Hiyoshi Shrine is Oyamakui and his wife Tamayorihime.{{Sfn|Breen|2009|p=161}}. The modern Sanno Festival, which is completely different from the Edo period, is based on the ``Hiyoshishanegiguchidensho'' {{Sfn|Breen|2009|p=161}}. The modern Sanno Festival since the Meiji period has become an event in which the couple deities Oyamakui and Tamayorihime interact to give birth to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamobetsu Raijin}} {{Sfn|Breen|2009|p=145}}.

=== Current enshrined deity ===
It consists of two main shrines and the following five sub-shas, which are called Hiyoshi Seven Shrines and Sanno Seven Shrines. The seven shrines are currently divided into the Nishi Hongu system and the Higashi Hongu system {{Sfn|Fukudome|2013|p=16}}.

* Tree Shrine: {{ill|Tamayori-hime|Q56344982|qid=Q56344982|lt=Kamo Tamayorihime God}}. Sessha of Higashihongu Shrine{{Sfn|Fukudome|2013|p=16}}
* Sannomiya Shrine: Kamo Tamayorihime no Mikoto Aratama - Kamo Tamayorihime no Mikoto Aratama. Sessha of Higashihongu Shrine{{Sfn|Fukudome|2013|p=16}}

* Hakusangu Shrine: {{ill|Kikurihime|Q11619891|qid=Q11619891}}. Sessha of Nishihongu Shrine{{Sfn|Fukudome|2013|p=16}}

=== Precincts ===
{{Attribute source|date=August 2025|section=1}}
* Nishihongu Main Hall ({{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|ar|كنز وطني ياباني|ca|Tresors Nacionals del Japó|de|Nationalschätze Japans|eo|Naciaj trezoroj de Japanio|es|Tesoro Nacional de Japón|fa|گنجینه ملی (ژاپن)|fi|Japanin kansallisaarteet|fr|Trésor national (Japon)|id|Pusaka Nasional (Jepang)|it|Tesoro nazionale del Giappone|ja|国宝|ko|일본의 국보|mr|राष्ट्रीय संपत्ती (जपान)|pt|Tesouro Nacional do Japão|ru|Национальные сокровища Японии|th|สมบัติแห่งชาติญี่ปุ่น|tr|Ulusal Hazine (Japonya)|uk|Національні скарби Японії|vi|Quốc bảo Nhật Bản|zh|日本國寶|qid=Q1139795}}) - Deity enshrined: {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōki no Kami}}. Rebuilt in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}}14 ({{ill|1586|Q6739|qid=Q6739}}). Renovated in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}}2 ({{ill|1597|Q6790|qid=Q6790}}). Kamishichisha (Sanno Shichisha). {{ill|Buddhist rites|Q45265996|qid=Q45265996}} were once held in the lower hall. The {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477|lt=cypress bark roofing}}, and the {{ill|Roof|Q83180|qid=Q83180}} is {{ill|Hiyoshi-zukuri|Q3138720|qid=Q3138720}}, a style unique to Hiyoshi Taisha Shrine. When viewed from the front, it looks like a {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|de|Irimoya|es|Tejado de gabletes de Asia oriental|fr|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|ko|팔작지붕|ru|Иримоя-дзукури|uk|Напіввальмовий дах|zh|歇山顶|qid=Q855025}}, but its distinctive feature is that the {{ill|Eaves|bew|Ceracapan|bg|Стряха|ca|Ràfec|ckb|گوێسەبان|cs|Okap|de|Dachtraufe|es|Alero (arquitectura)|et|Räästas|eu|Teilatu-hegal|fi|Räystäs|fr|Égout (architecture)|gd|Anainn|hi|ओलती|hsb|Skap|id|Tritisan|it|Gronda|ja|庇|kcg|A̱takncyiat|ko|처마|mk|Стреа|nds|Drüppenfall|pl|Okap (budownictwo)|pt|Beiral|sr|Стреха|sv|Takfot|tr|Saçak|uk|Звис|zh|屋簷|zh_yue|簷篷|qid=Q163972}} (eaves) at the center of the back are cut up, and this part is vertically cut off.
** Nishihongu Worship Hall ({{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}) - Rebuilt in 1586.

It is enshrined within the worship hall of Ushio Shrine.* Golden Rock (Kogane no Oiwa) - Also known as Golden Rock. * Okusoja - Deity enshrined: {{ill|Amatsukami and Kunitsukami|Q11442793|qid=Q11442793|lt=Tenjinjizi}}. The statue of Dengyo Daishi {{ill|Saichō|Q449943|qid=Q449943}} is enshrined here. It is the site of the former {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}}. It is also the place where Saicho's father, Momoe Mitsukubi, prayed for the birth of his child. It is located further into Mt. Hachioji.

=== Main festivals ===
[[Image:Hiyoshi Taisha Momiji 1.jpg|thumb|180px|Momiji Festival ({{ill|Light-up|Q17218409|qid=Q17218409}})]]
* Oto Opening Ceremony (January 1st) - This is the Saitan Festival, and before sunrise, under the light of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=torches}}, Nodayu Katayama performed the {{ill|Noh|Q226887|qid=Q226887}} performance at Nishimoto Shrine. (Noh)|Q11610440|Old Man}}' (Old Man of Hiyoshi), and {{ill|Yōkyoku|Q8062662|qid=Q8062662}}'{{ill|Takasago (play)|Q11672594|qid=Q11672594|lt=Takasago}}' is dedicated at Higashi Main Shrine.<ref name="jinjachou" /> It is also called ignition because there is a custom of taking the flame from the torch home and using it for cooking. 
* Sanno Festival (April 14) - It is said to have its origins around 1,300 years ago, when Miwa Myojin moved to Sakamoto, and the locals dedicated a large {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sakaki}}. The festival period lasts for one and a half months, including the raising of the mikoshi, the Oosakaki ritual, the horse ritual, the tea ceremony, the flower crossing, the Yoimiya ochi, the Awazu ritual, the return of the mikoshi, the Tori ritual, and the Funaro ritual. In particular, the mikoshi of the Sanno Seven Shrines is said to be magnificent, and contrasts with the silence of the Oosakaki ritual.* Sanno Worship Lecture (May 26th) - It is said that the origin of this tradition is that in the 2nd year of {{ill|Manju (era)|Q1194155|qid=Q1194155}} ({{ill|1025|Q19267|qid=Q19267}}), when it was lamented that monks were only working as {{ill|Sōhei|Q1475695|qid=Q1475695}} without training, the Lotus Hakkakko was held at the Nishimoto Shrine to enshrine Hiyoshi Okami<ref name="jinjachou" />. After the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=purification}} and the {{ill|Norito|Q1760119|qid=Q1760119}}, a question and answer session on the {{ill|Lotus Sutra|af|Lotussoetra|bg|Лотосова сутра|bn|সদ্ধর্ম পুণ্ডরীক সূত্র|ca|Sutra del Lotus|cs|Lotosová sútra|de|Lotos-Sutra|eo|Sutro de la blanka lotuso de la sublima darmo|es|Sutra del loto|et|Lootossuutra|fa|سوره نیلوفر|fr|Sūtra du Lotus|hi|सद्धर्मपुण्डरीक सूत्र|hu|Lótusz szútra|id|Sutra Seroja|it|Sutra del Loto|ja|法華経|ko|묘법연화경|lt|Lotoso sūtra|ms|Sutra Teratai|nl|Lotussoetra|no|Lotussūtraen|pa|ਸਧਰਮਪੁੰਡਰੀਕ ਸੂਤਰ|pl|Sutra lotosu|pt|Sutra do Lótus|ru|Лотосовая сутра|sr|Лотосова сутра|sv|Lotussutran|ta|தாமரை சூத்திரம்|th|สัทธรรมปุณฑรีกสูตร|tr|Lotus Sutra|uk|Сутра Лотоса|ur|سددھرمہ پونڈریکہ سوترم|vi|Pháp hoa kinh|wuu|妙法莲华经|zh|妙法莲华经|zh_yue|妙法蓮華經|qid=Q861212}} is held, and the Shiga Prefectural Shrine and Shrine Agency calls it ``a valuable festival that conveys to the present the state of the syncretization of Shinto and Buddhism.''<ref name="jinjachou" /> 
* Mitarashi Festival (July) - A {{ill|Ōharae-shiki|Q11261910|qid=Q11261910}} Shinto ritual <ref name="jinjachou" /> held at {{ill|Karasaki Shrine|Q11418537|qid=Q11418537}}, which is a separate shrine. The festival includes a grand purification ceremony, walking through a cogon grass ring, a puppet parade, and the burning of goma wood on {{ill|Lake Biwa|Q200239|qid=Q200239}}.<ref name="jinjachou" /> It is said to have divine virtues for diseases of the lower body and gynecological diseases. Furthermore, Karasaki Shrine is said to be one of the purification sites for Nanase.
* {{ill|Autumn leaf color|Q1156320|qid=Q1156320|lt=Momiji}} Festival (November) - In addition to various events, {{ill|light-up|Q17218409|qid=Q17218409}} is held throughout the Sakamoto area.
